difficulty_reason: The obligation replaces the quasi-polynomial chromatic bound for each fixed twin-width by a polynomial in clique number. The new human proof builds delayed decompositions and right-module partitions, controls clique growth in almost-mixed-free quotients, and inducts by lifting transversal corners through contraction and horizontal deletion. The external distinguishing vertices and separate mixed-zone arguments keep the induced restrictions within the lower-complexity classes; this is a substantive interacting research core beyond ordinary coloring and matrix-partition prerequisites.
scope_text: Select exactly the original Theorem 1.2: for every fixed natural \(t\), graphs of twin-width at most \(t\) have a polynomial chromatic bound in their clique number, with the polynomial depending on \(t\). The native introduction.tex 6 defines classes as hereditary, meaning closed under induced subgraphs. The full human delayed-decomposition, right-module, corner/contraction/horizontal-deletion, clique recurrence and all main almost-mixed-minor induction claims are retained. The ordinary cited twin-width/mixed-minor implication, Marcus--Tardos consequence and polynomial substitution closure have precise original statements and bibliography. Optional improved substitution exponents, mixed-extension and general right-extension claims remain unselected context; no extra unit is counted.
disclosure_text: The main lifting proof literally reuses \(t\): pcb\_tww.tex 32 uses it for the selected local modules \(L_1^\prime,\ldots,L_t^\prime\), while the earlier interval is \(I=\{v_s,\ldots,v_t\}\) at 14. Lines 34 and 39 then use the outside interval \(\{v_{t+1},\ldots,v_n\}\) and a witness with \(k>t\). The complete right-local-module definition, witness to the right of \(I\), extension instructions, corner/contraction/horizontal-deletion and both mixing arguments remain unchanged. No renamed index or editor lifting proof is supplied, and no broader contextual class claim is selected.
